hypothesis: Item 1.1's motivation: ST arrives ~2x hotter than SC, a single global EEG_SCALE cannot remove a per-cohort amplitude difference, so per-recording normalisation should close much of the cohort gap.
test: Per-recording kappa on the 44 held-out ST recordings against each recording's amplitude relative to the SC training median.
verdict: INCONCLUSIVE - the test has restricted range by construction
consequence: Item 1.1 keeps its motivation, but the motivation is now a HYPOTHESIS TO TEST rather than a diagnosis to act on. The measured signature of the cohort gap - a wake-specific precision collapse under a 3x prior shift, with recall intact across stages - is not what an input-scale mismatch would produce.
why_inconclusive: Every ST recording sits at 1.62-2.63x the SC training median; none is near 1.0x. So a within-ST correlation can only ask whether MORE shifted is worse, not whether the shift itself hurts - the whole cohort is displaced and there is no unshifted ST recording to contrast against. corr(kappa, |log amplitude|) = -0.247 is in the hypothesised direction but weak, and comparable in size to corr(kappa, wake fraction) = +0.297 pointing elsewhere. An earlier version of this file said NOT SUPPORTED on an arbitrary |r| < 0.3 threshold; that was an over-claim on an underpowered test.
what_would_settle_it: Run item 1.1 (per-recording normalisation) and re-measure the cohort gap. If amplitude is a real contributor the gap narrows; if it is not, the gap holds and the wake prior-shift account stands alone. That is one run and it is the only clean test available.
